lore.summary: The Proving Ground is where Frame pilots and vehicle crews from the Main Mech Hangar and the Long Store run live-fire and manoeuvre drills, on open ground east of the Gatehouse. A concrete bullet catcher at the north-east corner takes the impact of anything that overshoots a target. It is a separate facility from The Butts, which qualifies personnel on small arms -- this range is built for Frame- and vehicle-scale weapons, and nobody who has actually stood on either confuses them. Three small structures serve it: a ready hut near the gate where crews muster before a run, a control point partway down the range where the Range Safety Officer calls the line hot or safe, and a target shed near the backstop where silhouettes and scoring gear are kept and repaired.
lore.playerFacing: Open, flat, scraped ground with worn wheel ruts and a scatter of target frames, some standing and some knocked flat and not yet reset. A concrete wall looms at the far end, pocked and streaked, angled to catch anything that overshoots. A hut by the gate has a chalkboard nobody has wiped since the last rotation. Somewhere down-range, a loudspeaker crackles before anyone actually says anything into it.
lore.gmOnly: Treat this as the Frame-scale counterpart to The Butts, not a duplicate of it -- The Butts qualifies personnel on hand weapons, this range is built and rated for Frame and vehicle weapons, and mixing the two up in play will read as a mistake to anyone tracking the base's layout. The Range Safety Officer has real authority here: what a Frame's weapon can plausibly do to the backstop is a question for SF2E's own damage and area-effect rules, not GM fiat, so check before improvising a training accident. A technician-day cost for resetting targets or repairing backstop damage is reasonable and keeps this range competing for the same shared pool as everything else in campaign/config.json's frameEconomy.

hooks: A live-fire run goes wrong -- a target rig fails, a shot goes long, or a Frame's weapon does more to the backstop than anyone expected -- and the party is the nearest help.
The Range Safety Officer refuses to sign off on a Frame or a pilot for reasons they won't fully explain, and the party has to work out why.
A technician-day dispute over who gets the range this week -- qualification, repair testing, or someone's private practice -- lands on the party to referee or exploit.
activities: Run a live-fire or manoeuvre qualification, with the Range Safety Officer actually grading it.
Requisition range time for something off the training schedule -- testing a repaired Frame, or practising a manoeuvre nobody signed off on.
Help reset targets or assess backstop damage after a hard session, as real work with a real technician-day cost.
